$comment: Modules that were NOT type-clean when src/worker/lib became TypeScript.
Each carries a `// @ts-nocheck` header pointing here.
THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. A contract test asserts that the set of files
carrying @ts-nocheck is exactly the set named here, so adding one is a
deliberate edit somebody reviews rather than a quiet opt-out, and fixing a
module means deleting its entry. The counts are what tsc reported the day
the conversion landed, kept so progress is measurable rather than asserted.
THE ERRORS ARE NOT NEW DEFECTS. The code is byte-for-byte what shipped as
JavaScript and the staged bundle is byte-identical. What changed is the
checker: a .js file lets TypeScript treat every parameter as optional and
infer object shapes loosely, so TS2554 (arity) and TS2339 (unknown
property) were structurally invisible before. Those two are 97 of the 99.
19 of the 27 lib modules are clean and ARE fully checked from here on. That
is what this buys immediately, and it is why the answer was not to relax the
compiler for the whole directory.
THE CALLERS ARE A SEPARATE, TEMPORARY GROUP. Typing lib/ made TypeScript
check its call sites strictly, and 12 Worker modules that are still
JavaScript now fail against the signatures it infers. Their entries below
carry a .js extension and disappear as each module converts, so this half of
the list shrinks by construction rather than by anybody remembering.
